findings.title: GitHub Action reference points to a floating branch
findings.explanation: The workflow selects an action by a branch-like reference that can move without a workflow change. Other non-SHA version references are counted in inventory but are not findings in this conservative check.
findings.potential_impact: The referenced code may change while the workflow text remains unchanged, weakening review and reproducibility.
findings.remediation: Pin the action to a verified full commit SHA and use comments or Dependabot to track reviewed updates.

findings.title: ESP-IDF bootloader image validation is disabled
findings.explanation: A scanned Kconfig-style input or selected generated configuration explicitly enables CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_SKIP_VALIDATE_ALWAYS. ESP-IDF documents that this prevents the bootloader from validating the app image before booting it. This finding does not establish that the file is the active build configuration or that a built image is deployed.
findings.potential_impact: If this setting is active in a deployed build, a corrupted or modified app image may reach execution without the bootloader's normal image-validation step.
findings.remediation: Unset CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_SKIP_VALIDATE_ALWAYS unless a reviewed boot-time requirement justifies it. Verify the effective sdkconfig and resulting bootloader configuration for the release build.

findings.title: Private key PEM marker embedded in scanned file
findings.explanation: A PEM private-key boundary marker is present. FUSE detects the marker but does not validate the key or determine whether the file is deployed.
findings.potential_impact: If this is a usable private key shipped with a product, compromise of one copy may allow impersonation or decryption wherever that key is trusted.
findings.remediation: Remove the key from source and firmware, rotate or revoke it, and generate or provision unique keys through a protected process.

findings.title: ESP-IDF skips app-image validation after deep sleep
findings.explanation: A scanned Kconfig-style input or selected generated configuration explicitly enables CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_SKIP_VALIDATE_IN_DEEP_SLEEP. Espressif documents that this skips normal image checks, including checksum, SHA-256, and signature validation, when resuming from deep sleep. If the active OTA partition is changed before that resume, the new image may skip its first validation. This finding does not prove that the file is active or that the device follows that OTA/deep-sleep path.
findings.potential_impact: If the setting and OTA/deep-sleep sequence are both active, a modified app image may avoid the normal validation step on its first boot after the partition change.
findings.remediation: Keep image validation enabled when deep-sleep workflows can follow OTA partition changes. Review Secure Boot settings and verify the effective sdkconfig used for release builds.

findings.title: Credential-like literal in source
findings.explanation: A credential-related name is assigned a literal or compared with one. Quoted assignments and comparisons include C and C++ character-prefixed string literals. Plain values are also checked in .env files. FUSE cannot determine whether the value is valid or used.
findings.potential_impact: If the value is an active credential and the code or firmware is distributed, an unauthorized party may recover it and access the associated service or device.
findings.remediation: Remove the literal, rotate the value if it was exposed, and provision secrets through a deployment-specific secret store or protected device provisioning flow.
